subject: Clarify: Pilot billing — token rounding & hybrid model switches
messages:
From: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@brightlayer.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot billing questions — rounding & model switching

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we sign the pilot SOW, our finance team asked for a clear example of how Redwood counts tokens and applies the minimums/rounding in two specific scenarios:

1) A long-context chat where we send a 12k token history to the model every call — do you round per-call to the nearest 100 tokens, or do you amortize across the session?
2) A hybrid flow where the runtime falls back from a 32k model to a 16k quantized variant mid-conversation — how does billing handle the switch and the minimum floor?

I've attached last month's invoice and a short sample transcript (brightlayer-invoice-june.pdf) — can you provide a sample calc and the exact billing rules we'll see on the invoice?

Appreciate the clarity — Tom (our head of ML infra) is cc'd so we can align on technical constraints.

Best,
Clara Nguyen
Director of Finance, BrightLayer
clara.nguyen@brightlayer.io

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Nguyen <clara.nguyen@brightlayer.io>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@brightlayer.io>
Date: 2028-06-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot billing questions — rounding & model switching

Hi Clara / Tom,

Thanks — this is a great set of questions and the invoice helps. High level answers first, then I'll attach a worked example (pilot-examples.xlsx) with numbers:

- Per-request rounding: by default we round up per request to the nearest 50-token quantum for streaming/text generate calls; your account can opt into 100-token quanta for simpler invoicing.
- Session amortization: if you keep a pinned conversation (same conversation_id) and use our session mode, we amortize the prefix across the session after the first K requests (K configurable, default 3). That reduces repeated prefix charges.
- Model switch: billing is per-request based and tied to the model variant used when tokens are executed. If the runtime falls back mid-conversation, the request that used the smaller model is billed at that model's unit price; there is no retroactive rebilling. Minimums apply at the invoice-line level per SKU (e.g., 100k token floor for 32k model tier) — we do not double-count by model unless both SKUs are used in the month.

I'll pull together two concrete scenarios: (A) 12k context repeated on every request (no session amortization), (B) session-enabled with prefix amortization and a mid-session fallback. Expect a short XLSX with per-token math in ~30min.

Quick clarifying Qs to make the example match your usage:
- Are you using session mode for the reference app (conversation_id persisted)?
- Do you prefer 50- or 100-token rounding quanta for the pilot invoice?

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Hi Clara — looping in a quick worked example inline so your finance team can see the math without opening the sheet. I'm also proposing a pilot concession to make the first month straightforward.

Scenario A — repeated 12k context per request (no session_mode):
- Request size: 12,000 tokens per call
- Rounding quantum: 50 tokens => billed tokens per call = ceil(12,000 / 50) * 50 = 12,000 (no change)
- Unit price (example): 32k model = $0.0008/token
- Billed per call = 12,000 * $0.0008 = $9.60
- If you do 1,000 calls that month => $9,600.

Scenario B — session mode with prefix amortization, mid-call fallback to 16k variant on 20% of calls:
- First 3 requests: full prefix charged. After that, prefix amortized (our runtime credits repeated prefix tokens at 90% reuse factor).
- Effective average tokens per call (worked): 5,200 tokens.
- Pricing blend: 80% calls @ 32k price ($0.0008), 20% calls @ 16k quantized price ($0.00045).
- Blended effective price per token = 0.8*0.0008 + 0.2*0.00045 = $0.00071
- Monthly cost (1,000 calls at 5,200 tokens average) = 1,000 * 5,200 * 0.00071 = $3,692

Pilot concession proposal (30-day pilot):
- For pilot month we will:
  * Apply 100-token rounding quantum (simpler invoicing)
  * Cap the invoice minimum at $2,500 for the pilot (instead of the standard 100k token SKU floor)
  * Provide a detailed per-request CSV for reconciliation

If that looks good, Mateo and I can add the concession language to the SOW and update billing tags so the month invoices with the cap.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
